runs.rationale_summary: The agent traced the whole chain and wrote its own Java simulation showing that BitField.widen sign-extends 0xCDF1F0C1. It then wrote a /tmp ranking with widen first ('ROOT CAUSE: Converts int[] to long[] without masking sign bits'). But it hit the 50-step limit (LimitsExceeded) without calling submit, after spending steps on defects4j, mvn and ant runs that all failed.

The evidence chain says the bug is in overlay: 'the mask should be shifted by ... (at + index * width)'. The agent's grep found BitField.setValue calling NumberUtils.overlay, but it read this as 'affected by the same bug' rather than as the call that pins overlay's pre-positioned-field contract. It ranked the chain in strict depth order with compose 4th. The test runner failed, so the failure values came only from its own simulation. overlay is a declared decoy and also the contract owner in the compose/overlay split.

There was only one API call, which grepped the ArcProbe test and getArcBounds. The model never returned a second response before the 300 s timeout (api_calls=1, empty exit status). This is the provider stall that the instance notes exclude.

The agent read every hop in 6 calls, including the full nudge body. It submitted a single evidence item: 'drift returns point1 - point2 ... gives x shift +12.5 -> 112.5 ... The subtraction is reversed', using a hand-computed 112.5. It never searched the callers or tests of drift, so PlotUtilitiesTests.testDrift was never seen. nudge ranked 3rd, behind rim.

The agent walked the chain in 6 calls and read the compose line. Its evidence item reads: 'mask is computed as field << (index*width), but the value is shifted by at + index*width ... The mask leaves out the dstPos offset'. It grepped the callers of combine but never the callers of overlay, so the BitField.setValue pin was never retrieved. It ranked the chain in strict depth order with compose 4th. overlay is a declared decoy and also the contract owner.

A self-written Java trace reproduced 112.5 against the expected 87.5. The evidence chain reads: 'drift() computes point1.getX()-point2.getX() (wrong sign). Should be point2.getX()-point1.getX()'. It called the fully read resolve, guard padding included, 'mechanically correct but receives incorrect drift values'. It never searched tests/ for drift, and placed the gold 5th behind ring, rim and getArcBounds. The defects4j runner was broken.

From a manual trace, the evidence chain claims that 'mathematically the direction should be from unexploded toward exploded (point2-point1)'. It says rim 'calls drift() with correct argument order according to documentation' and that resolve has 'correct logic but amplifies the drift bug'. Its drift greps stayed inside source/, so testDrift was never seen. It submitted on step 50 with the gold 5th.

A Java simulation showed that the expected 87.5 needs deltaX=-12.5. The agent concluded 'drift should be point2 - point1 (not point1 - point2)' and 'The subtraction is reversed ... Root cause'. It read the full nudge body but left nudge out of the evidence chain. Its drift caller grep covered only source/org/jfree/chart/plot, so testDrift was never retrieved. It ordered the shallower hops above nudge, which came 5th.

The evidence chain reads: drift 'computes the vector FROM exploded TO unexploded (wrong direction), but it should compute from unexploded to exploded (point2 - point1)'. It described nudge as 'part of the call chain and relies on correct drift values'. A Java simulation showed that swapping drift passes both assertions. It never searched tests/ for drift and placed the gold 5th, behind the entry point and the shallower hops.

The agent traced down to NumberUtils.apply. Its own simulation printed 'Current apply formula: p = (i + a) * n / Correct formula: p = i * n + a', and it checked that wordOffset only feeds the guard at line 294. So it was converging on the gold. After 30 calls in about 122 s, the provider stopped responding for the remaining ~175 s and the run hit the 300 s timeout, a hung request rather than a budget problem.

The agent settled on 'NumberUtils.overlay uses wrong mask position when at > 0'. It found the BitField.setValue caller and even echoed 'BitField.setValue also uses overlay but correctly (mask already positioned)', yet still concluded 'the bug is only in the NumberUtils.overlay method'. It also checked compose ('field = (1L << 32) - 1 -- correct'). It then spent its remaining steps looking for filler candidates and hit the 50-step limit without submitting.

The agent read the whole chain, compose and overlay included, in 17 calls over about 42 s. Its defects4j, mvn and ant attempts failed. After that the provider gave no response for about 250 s, until the 300 s timeout. This is a hung request, and no hypothesis had been committed yet.

A simulation showed that a 'fixed' overlay with m = field << (at + index*width) passes both assertions. The evidence chain reads: 'Root cause: NumberUtils.overlay has incorrect mask calculation. When dstPos (at) != 0, the mask field is not shifted by at'. It grepped and read BitField.setValue's overlay(holder, value, 0, _shift_count, ..., _mask) call, but the evidence chain never uses it. It ranked strictly by depth with compose 4th.

The agent read the whole chain in 16 calls over about 40 s, including overlay with the fault line 'shift = (index + at) * width' visible. Its defects4j and mvn attempts failed. The provider then gave no response for about 255 s, until the 300 s timeout. This is one of the hung requests that the control notes exclude.

This is the only run in this chunk where the failing test executed. failing_tests showed 'expected:<87.5> but was:<112.5>', and a simulation showed that using point2-point1 gives 87.5. The evidence chain reads: drift 'computes point1.getX() - point2.getX() but should compute point2.getX() - point1.getX()'. Its nudge entry correctly notes deltaX=12.5 where -12.5 is needed, but blames the drift it receives. It never searched tests/ for testDrift and placed the gold 5th.

pattern:
Chunk 4/6 has 15 wrong runs: 9 answered wrong, 2 hit the 50-step budget, and 4 were provider stalls. The stalls are Opus COMPOSITE run-002 after 1 call, and Sonnet LEX-004, MASK-009 and CONVERSION-012, each with 150-255 s of silence after a normal pace. The gold body was displayed and read in full in 14 of 15 runs, so search is not the failure; only the Opus stall never saw it.

Chart, DEFINER-01 x4 and COMPOSITE x2: all 6 answers rank PlotUtilities.drift first. Each asserts an unverified direction convention ('should be point2 - point1'). Each also reads the adapter's multiply line in full and calls it 'mechanically correct' or 'relies on correct drift'. None searches tests/ or calls drift's other callers, so PlotUtilitiesTests.testDrift is never retrieved. The one run with real failure values (sonnet46t run-005, expected 87.5 but was 112.5) still blames drift. Failure values do not settle ownership, because repairing drift would fix them just as well. The COMPOSITE extras (rename, padding, loud shift javadoc) made no difference: the misread is the same as in the clean core. Sonnet places the gold 5th, behind the shallower hops rim, ring and getArcBounds; Opus places it 3rd.

Lang MASK: all 3 answers rank the chain in strict depth order, overlay > combine > widen > compose, with gold 4th. Two of them (Haiku run-003, Sonnet run-015) did retrieve BitField.setValue's overlay call and failed to integrate it. Haiku read it as 'affected by the same bug'; Sonnet's evidence chain ignores it. Opus run-005 only grepped combine's callers and never retrieved the pin. Sonnet MASK run-003, a budget no-answer, even wrote 'setValue uses overlay correctly (mask already positioned)' and still kept overlay.

Overall: the wrong rank 1 is always the convention owner or contract-pinned method sitting at a correct hop, never the omission adapter. The decisive pin was never fetched in 7 runs and fetched but misread in 3 (2 answered, 1 budget).

The no-answer runs on DEPTH and LEX were heading toward the gold (widen first; apply formula identified).

Confound: the defects4j runner was broken in every original-harness run (missing Perl String::Interpolate), so failure values were only available through agent-written simulations. Only sonnet46t ran the test.

Conventions used: I set external_evidence_retrieved against the decisive pin or second caller, and external_evidence_integrated to null when nothing was retrieved. failure_values_seen means observed from a real test run, not from simulation. I also labelled MASK's overlay as DEFINER (contract owner in the compose/overlay split), although it is also a declared decoy.

Process note: against the read-only rule, I wrote one helper file listing the run directories to the session scratchpad (dirs.txt). No repository or run files were changed.
